classification.difficultyReason: Calculate and compare two closed-cylinder surface areas, then justify the comparison.

content.prompt: Which shape has the larger surface area? Justify your answer.

spec.description: Wide upright closed cylinder, with a top-centre point and labelled radius to the right rim; height dimension outside the right silhouette. Decorative source shading omitted.
spec.mathematics: Radius 5 cm; height 3 cm. Both circular ends are included.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and shape label are visible.

spec.description: Tall upright closed cylinder, with a top-centre point and labelled radius to the right rim; height dimension outside the right silhouette. Decorative source shading omitted.
spec.mathematics: Radius 3 cm; height 5 cm. Both circular ends are included.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and shape label are visible.

answer.short: A has the larger surface area: $80\pi\text{ cm}^2$, compared with B's $48\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\mathrm A}&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\A_{\mathrm A}&=2\pi(5)^2+2\pi(5)(3)\\A_{\mathrm A}&=80\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\mathrm B}&=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\A_{\mathrm B}&=2\pi(3)^2+2\pi(3)(5)\\A_{\mathrm B}&=48\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$$
A has the larger surface area because $80\pi>48\pi$.
